bullets.text: Marcus cut funnel P95 from 2.8s to under a second; Priya shared it in the leadership channel.
Aman says Marcus's code reviews are the most useful he gets: 'picky but kind'.
On-call every third week for eight months; woken four times last rotation, three by the same flaky disk alert.
Concern that AI Insights is scoped to run an LLM nightly over every event stream, which is ~400M events a month for Globex alone.
Priority changes mid-sprint reach Marcus in standup rather than beforehand.
Strength: excellent technical judgment that people trust.
Growth area: judgment stays in Slack and hallways; if it isn't written down it doesn't shape the roadmap.
In the architecture review Marcus went quiet on Tom's caching pushback and then did it his way; disagree in the room or in writing.
For Priya: give a direct heads-up before standup when priorities shift.
Marcus wants staff engineer in the next cycle; he is at staff level on technical depth and close on developing others.
Scope evidence: lead the query engine migration with Aman, and Nina on the frontend switchover.
Promo packets due mid-January; Priya will advocate if the migration is on track with two or three solid docs.
Keep a decision journal for two weeks to adjust to less coding.
Kevin fixes or deletes the disk alert by October 2; Nina joins on-call next week.
Marcus writes a two-page AI Insights cost doc with Hannah's review by Wednesday the 1st, as a pre-read for Q4 planning.
Promo packet check-in in early December.
Regular 1:1 covering Marcus's concerns, feedback, and the staff engineer path.
On-call fatigue caused by a flaky, unowned disk alert.
Cost risk in the AI Insights scope and a cheaper precompute-anomalies approach (~99% cheaper).
Staff rubric: technical depth, scope, writing, developing others.
Speaking up in architecture reviews.
Writing is the main gap to staff; the AI Insights cost doc is the first step.
Cohorts rewrite moves to Aman so Marcus can lead the migration.
Cost doc by Wednesday the 1st; disk alert fixed by October 2; promo check-in in early December.
